Classic Cheese Blintzes

Served at: Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement)

Serves 6-8 (makes about 12-15 blintzes)Prep 30 min active, plus 30 min batter resting timeCook 45-60 min

Blintzes are delicate, thin crepes filled with a sweet cheese mixture, a beloved dish in Jewish cuisine. While often associated with Shavuot, they are also a popular and comforting choice for the pre-fast or break-fast meal on Yom Kippur, offering a gentle, dairy-rich sustenance before or after the solemn fast.

Ingredients

  • For the Crepes:
  • 1 cup (120 g) all-purpose flour
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 cup (240 ml) whole milk
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
  • 1 tablespoon (15 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 2 tablespoons (30 g) unsalted butter, melted, plus more for cooking
  • For the Cheese Filling:
  • 16 ounces (450 g) farmer cheese or well-drained ricotta cheese
  • 1 large egg yolk
  • 1/4 cup (50 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon lemon zest (optional)
  • For Serving:
  • Sour cream
  • Fruit preserves (e.g., cherry, blueberry)
  • Fresh berries

Method

  1. Prepare the crepe batter: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, eggs, milk, water, sugar, salt, and melted butter until smooth. The batter should be thin, like heavy cream. Cover the bowl and let it rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes (or up to 2 hours) to allow the flour to fully hydrate.
  2. While the batter rests, prepare the cheese filling: In a medium bowl, combine the farmer cheese (or drained ricotta), egg yolk, granulated sugar, vanilla extract, and lemon zest (if using). Mix until well combined and smooth. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired.
  3. Cook the crepes: Heat an 8-inch (20 cm) non-stick skillet or crepe pan over medium-low heat. Lightly grease the pan with a small amount of butter or oil. Pour about 1/4 cup (60 ml) of batter into the hot pan, immediately tilting and swirling the pan to evenly coat the bottom with a thin layer of batter.
  4. Cook the crepe for 1-2 minutes, or until the edges begin to curl and the top is set and no longer wet. Do not brown the crepe. Carefully loosen the edges with a spatula and invert the crepe onto a clean plate or cutting board, cooked side up. Repeat with the remaining batter, lightly greasing the pan as needed. Stack the cooked crepes as you go.
  5. Fill the blintzes: Lay a crepe cooked-side up on a clean surface. Place about 1 1/2 to 2 tablespoons of the cheese filling in the center of the crepe, forming a small log shape.
  6. Fold the sides of the crepe over the filling, then roll it up tightly from the bottom, creating a neat, rectangular package, similar to an envelope or spring roll.
  7. Repeat the filling and folding process with all remaining crepes and filling.
  8. Cook the filled blintzes: You can either pan-fry or bake them. For pan-frying, melt 1-2 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Place the blintzes seam-side down in the hot butter and cook for 3-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and heated through. For baking, preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Arrange blintzes in a single layer in a lightly greased baking dish, brush tops with melted butter, and bake for 15-20 minutes, or until heated through and lightly golden.
  9. Serve immediately with a dollop of sour cream, a spoonful of fruit preserves, and fresh berries.

Tips

  • For a smoother filling, you can press farmer cheese through a sieve or food mill before mixing.
  • Blintzes can be assembled ahead of time and refrigerated for up to 24 hours, or frozen unbaked for up to 1 month. If freezing, place them on a baking sheet until solid, then transfer to a freezer-safe bag.
  • Experiment with different fillings: add raisins, dried cranberries, or a touch of orange zest to the cheese mixture for variation.
